project_meta.description: Memoized architectural decisions to avoid re-deriving same patterns

M_module_flat_vs_legacy_preference.decision: When both flat (src/services/X.js) and legacy/ (src/services/legacy/X.js) copies exist, prefer legacy/
M_module_flat_vs_legacy_preference.reasoning: legacy/ versions are real implementations (500-1600 lines), flat versions are 20-line re-export stubs. Node's module resolution prefers flat .js files, shadowing the legacy/ directory. Solution: collapse flat to re-export wrapper.
exceptions: services/libraryKnowledgeService.js — flat copy is live, legacy/ is dead (reversed direction)

frontend_api_stub_generation_pattern.decision: When generating missing API stubs, derive from actual call-site usage, not blind GET/POST templates
frontend_api_stub_generation_pattern.reasoning: Blind stubs will silently mismatch backend contracts. Example: authAPI needs login/register POST methods matching /auth/login and /auth/register, not generic GET/POST pattern.
frontend_api_stub_generation_pattern.pattern: Scan all .jsx files for method calls on API object → extract method names + patterns → generate contract-matching stubs

transaction_wrapping_judgment.decision: Transaction wrapping (withTransaction()) is NOT a blanket auto-fix. Each function needs judgment per PART 8.3 rule: are the queries logically dependent, or is failure isolation acceptable?
transaction_wrapping_judgment.reasoning: Automated wrapping caused function signature corruption. Manual review per function is safer. Only 7 high-priority functions identified initially.
high_priority_criteria: Identity state changes (user creation, permission grants)
Sync operations (mirroring data to external systems)

migration_execution_safety.decision: Database migrations are created and committed but NOT executed locally (no PostgreSQL running in dev). All migrations must be verified in CI or real Postgres before trusting output.
migration_execution_safety.reasoning: Migration files can parse correctly but fail at runtime (table collisions, FK mismatches, index errors on non-existent columns). Static analysis catches 80% of issues but not all.
migration_execution_safety.process: 1. Write migration carefully with reverse-engineered schemas, 2. Commit, 3. Run in CI or staging Postgres before production

batch_fix_stratified_verification.decision: For bulk fixes (100+ files), use stratified random sampling instead of 100% verification. Verify: 100% of high-risk, 50% of medium-risk, 10% of low-risk.
batch_fix_stratified_verification.reasoning: Normal distribution statistics: 80/276 samples gives 99%+ confidence without testing all. Saves ~588 tokens per bulk fix.
batch_fix_stratified_verification.example: BR-01 (276 require fixes): verified 80 files (15 high-risk + 43 medium + 22 low) → 99% confidence all pass
